key_insight: Aligning a language model to embedding space (using the Embedding Language Model approach) allows opaque clinical-trial embeddings to be decoded into human‑readable descriptions and programmatically manipulated, enabling transparent exploration and generative uses.
problem_solved: Clinical-trial and general text embeddings are hard to interpret, explore, or invert, which limits transparency, validation, semantic search, and generative workflows in biomedical settings. ctELM provides tools to decode and manipulate those embeddings without requiring access to original training data.
method: Develop an open‑source, domain‑agnostic Embedding Language Model architecture that maps between embedding vectors and LLM token space.

Train the model on clinical‑trial embeddings with reconstruction and contrastive-style objectives plus domain-specific augmentations so embeddings can be decoded to descriptive text and edited in embedding space.
Expose decoding and manipulation primitives (embedding → text, text → embedding, embedding interpolation/perturbation) for search, explanation, and controlled generation.
impact: Practitioners gain practical tools to inspect, debug, and repurpose embedding spaces for better retrieval, interpretability, and synthetic data generation—while also needing to consider new privacy and inversion risks arising from reversible embeddings.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: embedding vector input → ELM alignment layer → LLM decoder (labels showing reconstruction/contrastive losses).
Embedding-space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) with points annotated by decoded trial summaries to show semantic neighborhoods and decoding fidelity.
Before/after examples: raw embedding → decoded trial title/criteria → edited embedding → generated variant trial text.
Pipeline flowchart: clinical-trial data → embeddings → ELM training → tools for decode/search/edit → downstream applications (retrieval, generation, auditing).
paper_title: ctELM: Decoding and Manipulating Embeddings of Clinical Trials with Embedding Language Models
paper_authors: Brian Ondov, Chia-Hsuan Chang, Yujia Zhou, Mauro Giuffrè, Hua Xu
